I can't give you a full 4x3 grid. #3b82f6 is a saturated blue, so most of the 12 OKLCH cells fall outside sRGB. Only 3 of the 12 can be displayed, and I left the other 9 empty rather than substitute clipped colors.

The grid is 4 lightness steps (rows, light to dark) by 3 chroma steps (columns, C ≈ 0.078, 0.188, 0.298). Hue is held at 259.8°. Contrast is OKCA with the shade as foreground on #ffffff. The pass threshold is ≥ 4.5.

| L (OKLCH) | C 0.078 | C 0.188 | C 0.298 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.873 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.623 | `#6b88b6` — 2.9 ✗ | `#3b82f6` — 2.9 ✗ (the base) | out of gamut |
| 0.373 | `#274069` — 9.2 ✓ | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.123 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |

Only `#274069` passes for body text on white. It is the darkest, lowest-chroma cell that exists. The base blue itself fails at 2.9, and it would pass only as large text or UI (≥ 3.0) if it were a touch higher, so at 2.9 it misses that too.

The in-gamut lightness range narrows as chroma rises. At C 0.188 the blue only exists between roughly L 0.47 and 0.65, so the very light and very dark rows can't be filled at any of the three chroma steps.

If you want a fully populated set, I can do one of these:
- **Adaptive grid:** `klar variants` without fixed steps returns only in-gamut cells, at the cost of a non-rectangular grid. On white, a few of its shades pass 4.5.
- **Lower-chroma grid:** I can pick chroma steps that all fit inside the gamut, for example 0.03, 0.07 and 0.12. That gives a full 4x3 grid, though it is less saturated than the brand blue.
- **Gamut-mapped cells:** I can fill the empty cells with the nearest displayable color, but those would not be the L/C values the grid claims.

Which would you like?

**Dark-mode primary: `#7bacfc`**

It scores OKCA 4.5 on `#1a1a2e`, foreground on background, which meets the AA body-text threshold. That is exactly the minimum, so it has no headroom.

**This costs some saturation, and that's your call.**
- The brand blue `#3b82f6` scores only 1.9 on the dark surface.
- Lightening it alone can't fix that. At its chroma (0.188), the brightest in-gamut version is L 0.648, and `find` tops out at 2.2 with `#438aff`.
- To reach 4.5 I had to drop chroma from 0.188 to 0.13 and raise lightness from 0.62 to 0.74. Hue is unchanged (~259.8°).
- The drift from the brand blue is deltaE 13, which reads as "clearly different" rather than a subtle dark-mode shift. It's the smallest change that passes, since `find` gives the closest compliant color.

**Alternatives:**
- **Keep `#7bacfc` for body text.** It's the closest color that passes. Use `#3b82f6` in dark mode only for large text or UI, where the threshold is 3.0. It scores 1.9 there today, so it still fails.
- **Lighten the dark surface.** A lighter `#1a1a2e` would let more of the brand blue's saturation survive. That changes the surface, though.

Only the pair `#7bacfc` on `#1a1a2e` was measured. Any other dark surface would need re-checking.

The `#` characters started comments, so I'll quote the colors.

Here are five accent colors for text on white. Each one passes body text (4.5) with OKCA measured as foreground on `#ffffff`, and all five look clearly different from each other.

| Accent | Hex | OKCA on white | Hue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crimson | `#c7013a` | 4.5 | red |
| Burnt orange | `#b24106` | 4.5 | orange |
| Green | `#027f36` | 4.6 | green |
| Blue | `#1754db` | 5.0 | blue |
| Magenta | `#a804ba` | 4.5 | magenta |

**Distinctness:** the closest pair is crimson and burnt orange at deltaE 18. Every other pair is 29 or more, and the guide treats 11 or more as clearly different.

**Margin:** four of the five sit right at 4.5, because I picked the smallest lightness change that reaches AA. That is the least drift from the original hues, but there is no headroom. If a token pipeline rounds or re-maps these colors, they could drop below 4.5. Say if you want a slightly darker set with a buffer.

**Drift from the base hues:** I started from common brand-style hues and only moved lightness where that was enough (blue). For the rest, lightness alone couldn't reach 4.5, so I let saturation drop slightly to get there. The resulting shifts from the starting colors are:
- Crimson: deltaE 7.
- Burnt orange: deltaE 14.
- Green: deltaE 13.
- Magenta: deltaE 7.
- Blue: deltaE 5.

The orange and green move the most, so they're the ones to check against your brand.

**Other hues I tried:** amber and teal also reached 4.5, but only as dark, muted colors (amber came out brownish, `#8e6001`). I left them out because the orange already sits in that hue range and looks more distinct.

I can add these as tokens in the repo if you want.

I checked all 6 foregrounds against both backgrounds with OKCA (foreground on background, body-text threshold 4.5). Of the 11 pairs, 4 pass and 7 fail. I re-measured every proposed fix, and all of them reach at least 4.5.

## Passing pairs
| Foreground | Background | OKCA |
|---|---|---|
| text `#1a1a2e` | surface `#ffffff` | 15.8 |
| muted `#666666` | surface `#ffffff` | 4.8 |
| inverse `#ffffff` | surface-dark `#1a1a2e` | 16.5 |

The `#1a1a2e` and `#ffffff` tokens sit on their own colors in two combinations, which I skipped as meaningless.

## Failing pairs and fixes
Each fix moves lightness only, keeping hue. ΔE is the perceptual change: under 3 is imperceptible, 5–10 noticeable, 11–20 clearly different, over 20 very different.

**On surface `#ffffff`**
| Foreground | Now | Fix | New OKCA | ΔE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary `#3b82f6` | 2.9 | `#115bcc` | 5.0 | 15 (clearly different) |
| accent `#e94560` | 2.8 | `#bf103f` | 4.7 | 13 (clearly different) |
| success `#22c55e` | 1.9 | `#047f38` | 4.6 | 22 (very different) |

**On surface-dark `#1a1a2e`**
| Foreground | Now | Fix | New OKCA | ΔE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary `#3b82f6` | 1.9 | `#7bacfc` | 4.5 | 13 (clearly different) |
| accent `#e94560` | 2.0 | `#fe8a93` | 4.6 | 14 (clearly different) |
| success `#22c55e` | 3.4 | `#41d870` | 4.8 | 5 (noticeable) |
| muted `#666666` | 2.4 | `#919191` | 4.7 | 17 (clearly different) |

## Decisions for you
- **Chroma cost:** primary and accent on dark, and success on white, can't reach 4.5 by lightness alone. Their in-gamut lightness range is too narrow, so klar's default search stopped short, at 2.2–2.8. The fixes above for those three pairs come from `--allow-desaturation`, which lowers saturation to get there. I applied that flag myself, so please confirm you're happy with those three:
  - success on white, `#047f38`: ΔE 22, a noticeably different green.
  - primary on dark, `#7bacfc`: ΔE 13.
  - accent on dark, `#fe8a93`: ΔE 14, which turns the coral toward pink.
- **Split tokens:** primary, accent and success each need a different value per background, because no single value passes on both. The light-surface and dark-surface variants above would be separate tokens.
- **Unintended pairs:** if `text` or `muted` never sit on the dark surface, those failures are moot. The same goes for `inverse` on white, which I didn't test since it is the same color. The ones that matter most are primary, accent and success on their intended backgrounds.
- **Unchanged:** I haven't edited `tokens-system.json`. I can apply whichever fixes you pick.
